reason: Eq. (3.43) gives "|c_{N}(nl)|^{-2}=\frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{\pi}d\theta\,\sin^{N-1}\theta\,(\phi_{nl}(\theta)^{2}+\psi_{nl}(\theta)^{2})". The claim leaves out the factor 1/2, but the relation it states is correct.

Eqs. (3.31)-(3.32) are coupled first-order differential equations in theta that link phi_{nl} and psi_{nl} at the same n ("[\frac{d}{d\theta}+...]\phi_{nl}=-(n+\frac{N}{2})\psi_{nl}"). The paper states no recursion in n.
Eq. (5.16) gives this exact heat kernel expansion on U/K.

Eq. (5.3) expands "\psi^{a}(x)=\sum_{\lambda\in\hat{U}(\tau)}\sum_{I}\sum_{\xi}\psi^{I}_{\lambda\xi}U^{\lambda}(\sigma^{-1}(x))^{a\xi}_{I}" as a sum over irreducible representations of U with coefficients psi^I_{lambda xi}.

Eq. (3.42) is the orthonormality of the S^{N-1} spinors \chi_{lm}^{(s)} ("\int_{S^{N-1}}d\Omega_{N-1}\chi_{lm}^{(s)\dagger}\chi_{l'm'}^{(s')}=\delta..."). The paper does not say the eigenspinors psi^{(s)}_{nlm} are orthonormal on S^{N-1}; their orthonormality is on S^N, in Eq. (3.41).
Eq. (5.16) writes the heat kernel in terms of the spherical functions \varphi_{\lambda}(x,y).

The paper says the spinor eigenfunctions on H^N "are obtained by analytically continuing those on S^N". The hyperbolic eigenfunctions come from the continuation, so the continuation does not use them as a technique.
Eq. (4.26) states "\hat{f}_{N}(y,t)={2^{N-3}\Gamma(N/2)\over\pi^{N/2+1}}\int_{0}^{+\infty}\phi_{\lambda}(y)e^{-t\lambda^{2}}\mu(\lambda)d\lambda" for the H^N heat kernel.
Eq. (3.69) gives "\theta\rightarrow iy, n\rightarrow-i\lambda-\frac{N}{2}", and the paper says "spinor eigenfunctions on H^N are obtained by analytically continuing those on S^N".
